name: port-peek
desc: Free, open-source port viewer for Windows — see which process listens on which port, kill it safely. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT.
features: ✅ **Live socket table** — TCP and UDP endpoints with local port, remote address and owning process
✅ **Process identity** — executable path and PID resolved automatically, no netstat dash-o guessing
✅ **Port conflict finder** — search any port number and see every claimant at once
✅ **Safe close action** — end one connection or the whole process with a confirmation naming the exe
✅ **New listener watch** — tray alert when an app starts listening, useful after installs
✅ **Filter presets** — LISTENING only, established only, or a saved filter for your dev ports
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, portable, offline, MIT with SHA-256 releases
compare: | Port conflict search | **Yes** | Manual | No | Manual |
| New listener tray alerts | **Yes** | No | No | No |
| Safe close with exe name | **Yes** | Yes | Partial | No |
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Zip | Zip | With OS |
faqQ: how to check which program is using a port on Windows?
faqA: netstat gives a PID you then have to match in Task Manager, which is slow every single time and worse in a hurry. port-peek resolves process names and paths next to each socket and can search by port to expose every claimant in one view. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline with SHA-256 releases.
